grades.A: Diagnostic accuracy established in dermatology-specific studies with reported sensitivity, specificity or likelihood ratios.
grades.B: Consistent textbook and guideline description; the direction of the effect is not in dispute, the magnitude is approximate.
grades.C: Calibrated estimate derived from Fitzpatrick's descriptive text and clinical convention. Directionally reliable, numerically soft. Adjust to your own case mix.
